title: Copper stocks rise alleviating backwardation and tightness fears
gist: A three-day, 63kt surge in on-warrant LME copper stocks has collapsed the cash-to-three-month backwardation from over $550/t to roughly $175/t, easing near-term tightness fears that had built through June and July, though tariff-driven arbitrage flows to the US remain a source of recurring dislocation risk.

insights.claim: On-warrant LME copper stocks rose 63kt over three days (a more than 50% increase), with the rise visible simultaneously in Asia, the US and Europe.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A rapid, globally synchronized inventory rebuild signals the acute nearby tightness that drove the backwardation spike is easing, reducing near-term squeeze risk for copper shorts and physical buyers.
insights.quote: On-warrant copper stocks have risen by 63kt over the last three days, a more than 50% increase.

insights.claim: Total LME copper stocks increased 28kt as deliveries flowed onto the exchange, with a significant amount of previously cancelled stock also being re-warranted.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Re-warranting of cancelled stock (material that had been earmarked for withdrawal) rather than only fresh deliveries suggests some of the apparent tightness was a positioning artifact, not a hard physical shortage.
insights.locator: Total stocks have pushed up 28kt with deliveries flowing onto the exchange

insights.claim: The LME copper cash-to-three-month spread fell sharply to around $175/t from over $550/t at points on the prior Monday, following the wave of exchange deliveries.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A backwardation collapse of this magnitude in days is an actionable signal for spread traders that the extreme nearby premium has largely unwound.
insights.locator: The deliveries caused the LME cash-to-three month spread to fall significantly

insights.claim: The LME three-month copper price stood at $13,885/t on Wednesday 19 August, down nearly $300/t since Monday, coinciding with the stock rebuild and backwardation unwind.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Price and spread moves together confirm the tightness premium, not just the term structure, is deflating - relevant for anyone pricing near-term copper exposure.
insights.locator: As of Wednesday 19 August, the LME three-month copper price is at USD 13,885/t

insights.claim: Benchmark copper analyst Albert Mackenzie says the recent deliveries alleviate fears of extreme nearby tightness for now, but LME inventories will remain the key signal to watch for further price direction.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Investors should treat LME on-warrant inventory levels as the near-term leading indicator for whether the copper squeeze re-emerges or continues to fade.
insights.quote: The deliveries alleviate the fears of extreme nearby tightness for now, and LME inventories will be closely watched for signals on price movements.

insights.claim: On-warrant copper stock fell 100kt across July and a further 75kt across June, driving the cash-to-three-month backwardation to close to $550/t, the highest level in over five years.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The scale and speed of the June-July drawdown explains why the backwardation reached a five-year extreme, giving investors a historical benchmark for how stretched the market had become.
insights.locator: on-warrant stock fell 100kt across July and 75kt across June

insights.claim: A significant share of the backwardation was concentrated in the front month, with more than $400/t of backwardation between the August and September contracts.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Front-month concentration points to a delivery-driven squeeze rather than a broad-based structural shortage, consistent with how quickly it unwound once deliveries arrived.
insights.locator: A significant amount of that arbitrage was in the front month

insights.claim: Market sources told Benchmark they believe one large trading company was behind the recent deliveries, while sources in China believe some deliverers may have been Chinese market participants.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: If a single large trader or Chinese participants are driving the delivery flow, the unwind could reverse quickly if that specific flow pauses - worth tracking counterparty concentration risk.
insights.locator: Sources noted to Benchmark that they believed one large trading company

insights.claim: Mackenzie attributes much of the unusual copper market dynamics to large volumes of copper flowing to the US on tariff-arbitrage, which makes the global market appear tighter than it really is, and warns similar episodes could recur while tariff uncertainty persists.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: As long as US tariff policy on copper remains uncertain, investors should expect recurring bouts of artificial ex-US tightness and backwardation spikes driven by arbitrage flows rather than genuine global scarcity.
insights.quote: Lots of the current odd dynamics have come as huge amounts of copper heads to the US due to the high arbitrage caused by tariff uncertainty, making the global market feel tighter than it really is.
insights.locator: quote from Mackenzie on tariff-driven flows
